title: The Year of Mercy (2015–2016)
hook: a jubilee where Doors of Mercy opened in cathedrals around the world, not only in Rome

segments.voice: Yesterday, Francis, the Jesuit who took the name of the poor man of Assisi. Your line was a poor church for the poor. How did your simple thing go? Day nine hundred thirty-four.

A heavy door, usually sealed shut, swings open, and people start walking through it. Slowly, some touching the frame, some carrying children, some in wheelchairs pushed by friends. It's only a doorway. On the other side is the same church floor. But in a jubilee year, walking through a Holy Door is a pilgrimage in a few steps. The best-known Holy Doors are in Rome's great basilicas, and to walk through one of those you had to get there. Then Pope Francis called a jubilee and asked that doors like this be opened in cathedrals and shrines everywhere, so that people who could never travel to Rome could walk through one at home.
screen: `A SEALED DOOR SWINGS OPEN.` → `A PILGRIMAGE IN A FEW STEPS.` → `NOT ONLY IN ROME.`

segments.voice: The year rested on four things. First, the opening line. Francis announced the jubilee in a document named for its first words, Misericordiae vultus, the face of mercy. It begins by saying that Jesus Christ is the face of the Father's mercy. Second, the motto: merciful like the Father. It comes from Luke, in the Douay-Rheims: "Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful." Third, the door. Jesus says in John's Gospel, "I am the door. By me, if any man enter in, he shall be saved." The Holy Door is that line made into wood and hinges. The document asked that a Door of Mercy be opened in the cathedral of each diocese, and could also be opened at other churches and shrines. Walking through it, with confession and prayer, was a way of receiving the jubilee's grace, the indulgence. Fourth, the works. The document asked Catholics to rediscover the works of mercy. The corporal ones: feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, clothe the naked, welcome the stranger, heal the sick, visit the imprisoned, bury the dead. And the spiritual ones, among them: counsel the doubtful, comfort the afflicted, forgive offenses, bear wrongs patiently, pray for the living and the dead. Francis also sent out priests he called Missionaries of Mercy, to preach and to hear confessions. The door was the symbol; the works were the point. A door you walk through in a few seconds, and then a whole list of things to do on the other side.
screen: `THE FACE OF MERCY.` · `MERCIFUL LIKE THE FATHER.` · `I AM THE DOOR.` · `THE WORKS OF MERCY.` · then, large: `BE YE THEREFORE MERCIFUL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: walk through a church door as a prayer, or get ready to. Settle, and breathe. If there's a church near you, picture its door: the handle, the weight of it, the step down or up. If not, picture any doorway you pass through every day. Choose one work of mercy from the list, the one you'd most like to have done for you. Then imagine walking through that door carrying it. If you pray, you can say the line from John, I am the door. If you don't, just let the doorway mean something today. The bell holds the time.
Misericordiae vultus. The face of mercy, the document in which Pope Francis announced the Year of Mercy and asked that Holy Doors be opened in cathedrals everywhere.
Your line: the door of mercy. Today, every time you go through a door, let it remind you of the work of mercy you chose, and do it once. Day nine hundred thirty-four.

howItsDone: In a jubilee year Catholics make pilgrimage through a Holy Door, usually with confession, Communion and prayer for the pope's intentions; the works of mercy are taught in parishes and practiced through parish outreach.

notes: Claims rule: no dates spoken. The outline hook's 'in every diocese' is phrased as what the bull asked ('the cathedral of each diocese'), which Misericordiae vultus says; confirm.
'For a long time the Holy Doors people talked about were in Rome' is a general historical claim; Keeper may soften or cut. ('famous' is descriptive, not a ranking.)
Lists of corporal and spiritual works of mercy as given in Misericordiae vultus §15 (spiritual list given in part); confirm wording.
Missionaries of Mercy: confirm description from the bull §18.
Indulgence conditions in howItsDone (confession, Communion, prayer for the pope's intentions): confirm.
Douay-Rheims Luke 6:36 and John 10:9 wording: confirm exactly.
Editor: works of mercy list now follows Misericordiae vultus wording ('heal the sick, visit the imprisoned'); removed the 'for Catholics' generalization in the hook; varied the teach opener.
Auditor: 'for a long time the Holy Doors were in Rome' overstated it (Santiago de Compostela, for one, has its own Holy Door); now limited to Rome's basilicas being the best known; Keeper may cut.
